mainTopic: The טריפות of a bird, and how to check whether a weasel's bite on the head pierced the membrane of the brain
overview: This amud opens with the last line of a ברייתא: the skin of the בית הבושת counts like meat for פיגול and כרת. Then a new משנה lists the injuries that make a bird a טריפה, such as a pierced gullet, a cut windpipe, a weasel's blow to the head, and singed innards that turned green. A crushed bird that lives a full 24 hours is kosher. The גמרא begins with the head injury. רב, שמואל and לוי teach that you press the brain from inside, and if it bulges out through the skull the bird is a טריפה. זעירי first says a weasel bite cannot be checked at all because its teeth are thin and crooked, but later he takes this back. He reports that רבי שמעון בן לקיש allows checking by hand but not with a nail, while רבי יוחנן allows even a nail. The same argument is traced to רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה. Three times a teaching of לוי, that a broken skull makes a bird טריפה even when the membrane is whole, is answered the same way: it refers only to a water bird, whose membrane is soft. The amud ends with practical ways different sages checked the membrane, and the list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: the skin of the בית הבושת and פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list. The skin of the בית הבושת is treated like meat: wrong-place intent makes it פסול without כרת, and wrong-time intent makes it פיגול with כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes to include the skin of the vulva. If the intent was to eat it outside its proper place, the offering is unfit but there is no כרת. If the intent was for beyond its proper time, it is פיגול and one is liable to כרת for eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא that started before this section. The last item it lists is the skin of the בית הבושת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats this skin exactly like the meat of the offering. Wrong intent about place only makes it פסול. Wrong intent about time creates פיגול, which carries כרת. The גמרא uses this to show which תנא counts certain skins as meat, which backs up what רבי יוחנן said earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: The skin of the private area of a female animal
Intent to eat or burn the offering outside its proper place
Intent to eat or burn the offering after its proper time
An offering made invalid by intent to eat it after its proper time; eating it carries כרת

steps.whatToRemember: Intent for the wrong place makes it פסול with no כרת. Intent for the wrong time makes it פיגול with כרת. Here the skin of the בית הבושת follows the same rules as meat.

phrases.english: To include the skin of the vulva
phrases.notes: This is the end of a list that started before this section. The ברייתא is adding one more skin that counts like meat.

phrases.english: With intent for outside its place, it is unfit
and there is no כרת for it,
with intent for beyond its time, it is פיגול
and one is liable to כרת for eating it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא quoted in the previous section to support רבי יוחנן
steps.raayaObject: That certain skins are treated like meat for פיגול and כרת according to one תנא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that lists skins which count like meat

steps.title: The משנה lists the injuries that make a bird a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists bird טריפות: a pierced gullet, a cut windpipe, a weasel's blow to the head, a pierced gizzard, pierced small intestines, and innards singed in fire if they turned green.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the טריפות in a bird: a pierced gullet, a cut windpipe, a weasel striking its head in a spot that makes it a טריפה, a pierced gizzard, and pierced small intestines. If the bird fell into a fire and its innards were singed, it is unfit if they are green and kosher if they are red.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It focuses on birds and lists the injuries that make a bird a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of these injuries are found in animals too, but some are special to birds, like the gizzard. The weasel case is about a blow that may have pierced the membrane of the brain. The fire case depends on color: green innards show real damage, while red innards are still healthy.

keyTerms.meaning: Injuries that make a bird non-kosher even if it is slaughtered properly
The gizzard, a muscular stomach found in birds
Were singed or heated by fire

steps.confusionAlert: For the gullet, any hole is a problem. For the windpipe, the משנה says 'cut', meaning cut across, not just a small hole.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are the טריפות in a bird:
one with a pierced gullet,
and one with a cut windpipe,
if a weasel struck it on its head
in a spot that makes it a טריפה,
if the gizzard was pierced,
if the small intestines were pierced,
if it fell into the fire
and its innards were singed,
if they are green, they are unfit,
if they are red, they are kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins and moves from קדשים to bird טריפות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The listed injuries make a bird a טריפה. Singed innards depend on color: green is unfit, red is kosher.

steps.title: A crushed bird that survives 24 hours
steps.stepSummary: A bird that was trampled, slammed against a wall, or crushed by an animal and is twitching is a concern. But if it lives a full 24 hours and is then slaughtered, it is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone trampled the bird, or slammed it against a wall, or an animal crushed it, and it is twitching, and it lived for a full day and night and then he slaughtered it, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a crushed bird. It teaches that surviving 24 hours shows the bird is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushing raises the worry that its limbs or organs were shattered inside, which would make it a טריפה. If the bird lives through a full 24 hours, that proves it was not fatally damaged. So it may be slaughtered and eaten.
steps.whatToRemember: A crushed bird that lives through a full 24 hours and is then slaughtered is kosher.

phrases.english: If he trampled it, or slammed it against a wall
or an animal crushed it
and it is twitching,
and it lasted a full 24 hours
and he then slaughtered it, it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה with a crushed bird whose outcome depends on survival
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A crushed, twitching bird that survives 24 hours and is then slaughtered is kosher.

steps.title: How to check a bird struck on its head
steps.stepSummary: רב, שמואל and לוי teach the check for the weasel case. You put your hand inside and press. If the brain bulges out through the hole, it is a טריפה; if not, it is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב, שמואל and לוי say: He puts his hand inside and checks. If the brain bulges out and rises, it is a טריפה. If not, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the weasel case in the משנה. It teaches a practical way to tell whether the brain's membrane was pierced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The membrane around the brain normally holds the brain in place. If pressing from below pushes brain matter out through the hole in the skull, the membrane must be torn, so it is a טריפה. If nothing comes out, the membrane is whole.

keyTerms.meaning: He puts his hand inside the bird

phrases.english: GEMARA: רב and שמואל and לוי, who say:
he puts his hand inside and checks,
phrases.notes: He reaches in through the bird's mouth and presses the brain up from below with his finger.

phrases.english: if it bulges out and rises, it is a טריפה,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the brain matter, pushing out through the hole the weasel made in the skull.

phrases.english: and if not, it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to apply the weasel case from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Press the brain from inside. If it bulges out through the skull, it is a טריפה; if not, it is kosher.

steps.title: Does the check work if only the outer membrane was pierced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the check fits the view that only piercing the inner membrane makes a טריפה. But by the view that piercing the outer membrane alone is enough, maybe the outer one is pierced while the inner holds the brain in.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says it is not a טריפה until the lower membrane is pierced. But for the one who says it is a טריפה once the upper membrane is pierced, even if the lower is not, let us worry: maybe the upper was pierced and the lower was not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the check of רב, שמואל and לוי. It may fail according to one view about the brain's two membranes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brain has two membranes. If only the inner one counts, the bulging check works well. But if piercing the outer one alone makes a טריפה, the whole inner membrane would still hold the brain in. Then the check would wrongly show the bird as kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to the one who says

steps.confusionAlert: The 'upper' membrane is the outer one, right under the skull. The 'lower' membrane is the inner one, touching the brain.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
phrases.notes: The argument about the two membranes appears earlier in this מסכת, on דף 45a.

phrases.english: it is not a טריפה until the lower membrane is pierced,
but according to the one who says that if the upper membrane was pierced,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אִינְּקִיב תַּתָּאָה,
phrases.english: even though the lower was not pierced, it is a טריפה,
let us worry that perhaps the upper was pierced
and the lower was not pierced?
phrases.notes: In that case no brain would bulge out, but the bird would still be a טריפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר עַד דְּמִנְּקִיב קְרָמָא תַּתָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the check from step 4 works for every opinion
steps.kashyaTarget: The bulging-brain check of רב, שמואל and לוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If piercing the outer membrane alone makes a טריפה, a whole inner membrane could keep the brain from bulging out, so the check would miss a real טריפה.

steps.title: The soft inner membrane always bursts too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if the outer membrane were pierced, the inner one is so soft it would surely burst as well. So the check is reliable by every view.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the upper membrane really were pierced, the lower one, because it is so soft, would certainly burst.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps the check of רב, שמואל and לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner membrane is too fragile to hold up once the outer one is torn. So a pierced outer membrane always comes with a burst inner one, and the brain will bulge out. If nothing bulges, both membranes must be whole.
steps.whatToRemember: The bulging-brain check works by every view. A torn outer membrane always leads to a burst inner one, because the inner membrane is so soft.

phrases.english: If it were so that the upper membrane was pierced,
the lower one, because of its softness, would certainly burst.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: A physical fact: a pierced outer membrane always means a burst inner membrane, because the inner one is so soft
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outer membrane could be pierced while the inner one stays whole and holds the brain in
steps.terutzMaskana: The soft inner membrane always bursts once the outer one is pierced, so the check catches every טריפה

steps.title: זעירי: The weasel bite cannot be checked
steps.stepSummary: זעירי rules that the check for a weasel bite does not work, because the weasel's teeth are thin.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: There is no check for a weasel bite, because its teeth are thin.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion comes in. זעירי says the press-the-brain check from רב, שמואל and לוי does not work for a weasel bite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said you press, and if the brain bulges out, the bird is a טריפה. זעירי worries that thin teeth make holes so tiny that nothing bulges out even when the membrane is pierced. So by his view a passed check proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A check or inspection to see whether the animal is a טריפה
A weasel; here, a weasel that bit the bird on the head

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said:
There is no check for a weasel [bite],
phrases.notes: He means the pressing check from רב, שמואל and לוי a few steps back.

phrases.english: because its teeth are thin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the check taught in step 4 and says it does not work for a weasel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A weasel bite on the head cannot be checked, because the weasel's teeth are thin.

steps.title: Why should thin teeth matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions זעירי's reason: a thin hole is still a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if its teeth are thin, what difference does that make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on זעירי's reason. Even through a small hole, some brain should still bulge out when you press.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is aimed at the reason, not at the ruling itself. If a hole exists, pressing should push something through it, however small. So 'thin teeth' alone does not explain why the check fails.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?

phrases.english: And if its teeth are thin, what of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason זעירי gave in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's reason that thin teeth make the check useless.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A small hole is still a hole, so pressing should still push some brain through it.

steps.title: רב אושעיא: The teeth are thin and crooked
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא adds that the teeth are also crooked, so the holes don't line up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: It is because its teeth are thin and crooked.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא answers the question by adding one more detail: the weasel's teeth are crooked as well as thin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A crooked tooth makes a hole in the skull and a hole in the membrane that are not in the same spot. Then the brain has no straight path out, so nothing bulges even if the membrane is pierced. That is why the check cannot be trusted.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said:
Because its teeth are thin and crooked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשִּׁינֶּיהָ דַּקּוֹת וַעֲקוּמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8 by sharpening זעירי's reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a missing detail to the reason (crooked, not just thin).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Thin teeth alone would still leave a hole the brain could bulge through.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thin and crooked teeth leave holes that don't line up, so the brain may not come out even when the membrane is pierced.

steps.title: זעירי takes it back: Hand check yes, nail check disputed
steps.stepSummary: In נהרדעא זעירי retracts his ruling. He reports that רבי שמעון בן לקיש allows a hand check but not a nail, and רבי יוחנן allows even a nail.
steps.simpleTranslation: When זעירי went up to נהרדעא, he sent them a message: What I told you was my mistake. Rather, this is what they said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: You check a weasel bite by hand, but not with a nail. And רבי יוחנן says: even with a nail.
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי withdraws his earlier ruling that no check works. He replaces it with a dispute between רבי שמעון בן לקיש and רבי יוחנן about which tools you may use to check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now everyone agrees a check does work. The new question is the method. רבי שמעון בן לקיש allows only pressing by hand, since a nail might itself pierce the membrane. רבי יוחנן allows running a nail over the membrane to feel for a hole.

keyTerms.meaning: They are a mistake on my part (a sage taking back his own ruling)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a sage openly taking back his ruling. It also moves the discussion from 'can you check at all?' to 'how may you check?'.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. רבי שמעון בן לקיש says hand only, NOT a nail. רבי יוחנן says even a nail is fine.

phrases.english: When he went up to Neharde'a,
he sent to them:
The things that I said before you
are a mistake on my part.
But this is what they said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
One checks a weasel [bite] by hand,
but not with a nail.
And Rabbi Yochanan says: even with a nail.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלֵיק לִנְהַרְדְּעָא, שְׁלַח לְהוּ: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָמַרְתִּי לִפְנֵיכֶם טָעוּת הֵן בְּיָדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: זעירי himself withdraws the ruling of steps 7-9 and replaces it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A weasel bite may be checked. By hand everyone agrees. With a nail, רבי שמעון בן לקיש forbids it and רבי יוחנן allows it.

steps.title: The same argument between רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this dispute also appears between רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה. One checked by hand and one with a needle, and each criticized the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is also the argument of רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה. One checked by hand and one checked with a needle. The one who checked by hand said to the one who checked with a needle: How long will you waste the money of the Jewish people? The one who checked with a needle said to the one who checked by hand: How long will you feed the Jewish people נבלות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the hand-versus-tool argument already existed between earlier sages. Each side gives a sharp reason why the other's method is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hand-checker says the needle may itself pierce a whole membrane. Then good kosher birds get thrown out, which wastes people's money. The needle-checker says a hand check can miss a real hole, so forbidden birds get eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute, an argument between sages
Wasting the money of the Jewish people (making them throw out kosher food)
Animals that died without a proper שחיטה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the two worries that run through all checking questions. One is being too strict and wasting kosher food. The other is being too lenient and letting people eat forbidden food.

phrases.english: And [this is] in the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Nechemya:
one checked by hand,
and one checked with a needle.
The one who checked by hand
said to the one who checked with a needle:
Until when will you waste
the money of the Jewish people?
phrases.notes: If the needle makes a hole itself, a kosher bird gets thrown away.

phrases.english: The one who checked with a needle said to him,
to the one who checked by hand:
Until when will you feed
carcasses to the Jewish people?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the dispute in step 10 already existed between earlier sages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה argued about checking by hand or with a needle. Each side warned of the other's danger: wasted kosher food, or forbidden food being eaten.

steps.title: How can a slaughtered bird be called נבלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the word 'נבלות', because this bird had a proper שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Carcasses? But it was slaughtered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops on one word in the needle-checker's complaint. A bird that had a proper שחיטה cannot be a נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבלה is an animal that died without a valid שחיטה. This bird was slaughtered properly. Even if it is forbidden, the most it could be is a טריפה, never a נבלה.

phrases.english: Carcasses?
But it is slaughtered!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one word in the needle-checker's complaint in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'נבלות' in the needle-checker's complaint.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A properly slaughtered bird can never be a נבלה, so the word cannot be right.

steps.title: Read it as טרפות: the membrane may be pierced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the word to 'טרפות'. The fear is that the brain's membrane was pierced and the hand check missed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said טרפות, because perhaps the membrane of the brain was pierced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording: the needle-checker meant טרפות, not נבלות. It also states his worry plainly: the hand check might miss a pierced brain membrane.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird had a valid שחיטה, so the only possible problem is that it is a טריפה. The needle-checker fears the hand check is not enough. The brain might not bulge out even though the membrane is pierced, which echoes the thin, crooked teeth from step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals forbidden because of a fatal injury, even with a proper שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: זעירי at first said no check works for a weasel bite, then took it back. רבי שמעון בן לקיש allows checking by hand but not with a nail, and רבי יוחנן allows even a nail. רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה had the same argument: one checked by hand and one with a needle. The hand side fears wasting kosher food, and the needle side fears that a hand check misses a real טריפה.

phrases.english: Rather, [say] tereifot,
perhaps the membrane of the brain was pierced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טְרֵפוֹת, שֶׁמָּא נִיקַּב קְרוּם שֶׁל מוֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12 by correcting the word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the wording of the quoted statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The needle-checker seemed to call the birds נבלות.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant טרפות. A hand check might miss a pierced brain membrane.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יהודה is the one who checks by hand
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה says to check by hand and not with a nail, so he is the one who checks by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can prove that רבי יהודה is the one who checked by hand. A ברייתא says in his name: you check a weasel bite by hand, not with a nail. If the bone broke, even if the brain membrane was not pierced, the bird is טרפה. Yes, it is proven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles which of the two תנאים from Step 11 checked by hand. A ברייתא in רבי יהודה's name says 'by hand,' so it was him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11 we only knew that one of רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה checked by hand and the other used a needle. This ברייתא states רבי יהודה's view outright, so רבי נחמיה must be the one who used the needle. The second line of the ברייתא, about a broken bone, will cause trouble in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It can be concluded, it is proven
A weasel, the animal that bit the bird's head
A nail, a sharp tool used for checking
The thin membrane that covers the brain

phrases.aramaic: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הוּא דְּבָדֵיק בִּידָא,
phrases.english: It may be concluded that it is Rabbi Yehuda who checks by hand,
phrases.notes: This goes back to Step 11, where we didn't know which of the two checked by hand.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹדְקִין לְחוּלְדָּה בַּיָּד, אֲבָל לֹא בְּמַסְמֵר.
phrases.english: One checks a weasel bite by hand, but not with a nail.

phrases.aramaic: נִשְׁבַּר הָעֶצֶם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִיקַּב קְרוּם שֶׁל מוֹחַ –
phrases.english: If the bone broke, even though the brain membrane was not pierced,
phrases.notes: The ruling isn't spelled out here, but it means the bird is טרפה.

phrases.english: It is proven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הוּא דְּבָדֵיק בִּידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the unnamed sides of the dispute in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה is the one who checks by hand.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in רבי יהודה's name.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The first line allows checking, but the second line makes a broken skull טרפה even when the membrane is whole, which means checking does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. You said: check a weasel bite by hand, not with a nail. So checking works. Then it says: if the bone broke, even if the membrane was not pierced, it is טרפה. So checking does not work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the two halves of the same ברייתא seem to clash with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you are allowed to check, then the membrane is what matters, and a whole membrane should make the bird kosher. But the second half says a broken bone alone makes it טרפה even with a whole membrane. Then there would be nothing to check for.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult, it contradicts itself
Checking, the option to inspect and permit
And then it goes on to teach

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ: בּוֹדְקִין לְחוּלְדָּה בַּיָּד אֲבָל לֹא בְּמַסְמֵר.
phrases.english: You said: One checks a weasel bite by hand, but not with a nail.
Apparently, it can be checked,
and then it teaches: If the bone broke,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִיקַּב קְרוּם שֶׁל מוֹחַ.
phrases.english: even though the brain membrane was not pierced, it is טרפה.
Apparently, it cannot be checked!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in רבי יהודה's name.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Its first clause allows checking the membrane, while its second clause makes the bird טרפה no matter what the membrane looks like.

steps.title: The second half is about a water bird
steps.stepSummary: The second line talks about a water bird, which has no membrane to check.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second half is about a water bird, since it has no membrane.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two halves deal with different birds. The broken-bone rule is only for a water bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a regular bird you can check the membrane by hand. For a water bird there is nothing reliable to check, so a broken skull alone makes it טרפה. The very next step will question the words 'no membrane.'

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause, the end part of a teaching

phrases.english: In the latter clause, we have come to a water bird,
since it has no membrane.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction by splitting the two clauses into different cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each clause deals with a different kind of bird.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses were about the same kind of bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is about a regular bird and the second clause is about a water bird.

steps.title: Does a water bird really have no membrane?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the claim that a water bird has no membrane at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think it has no membrane?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the wording of the answer it just gave. It is not reasonable to say a water bird has no brain membrane at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A water bird plainly does have a membrane, so the wording 'no membrane' can't be right. This sets up a correction of the wording in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (a way of rejecting an idea)

phrases.english: Can it enter your mind that it has no membrane?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the answer just given.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'since it has no membrane.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Anyone can see that a water bird has a brain membrane.

steps.title: Correction: its membrane is soft
steps.stepSummary: The wording is fixed: the water bird's membrane is soft, so it surely tore when the skull broke.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since its membrane is soft.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא corrects the wording of its answer. The point is not that there is no membrane, but that the membrane is soft.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A soft membrane under a broken skull is assumed to be damaged even if you can't see it, so checking does not help. That is why the broken bone alone makes a water bird טרפה.
steps.whatToRemember: A regular bird bitten on the head can be checked by hand. A water bird with a broken skull is טרפה even if the membrane looks whole, because its membrane is soft.

phrases.english: Rather, since its membrane is soft.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes the wording that was questioned in Step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The water bird has no membrane at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The water bird has a soft membrane that is assumed damaged once the skull breaks.

steps.title: רב נחמן challenges רב ענן with לוי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks how שמואל and רב can permit after a hand check, when לוי teaches that a broken skull makes a bird טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב ענן: You say that שמואל checks by hand and permits, and our friend הונא says that רב checks by hand and permits. But לוי teaches: the טרפות the חכמים listed for an animal apply to a bird too, and a bird has one more: a broken bone, even if the brain membrane was not pierced!
steps.whatsHappening: The same question now comes up in a talk between two אמוראים. רב נחמן challenges the hand-check rule of רב and שמואל using a ברייתא of לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רב and שמואל permit a bird after a hand check shows the membrane is whole. לוי's ברייתא says a broken skull alone makes a bird טרפה, which seems to leave no room for checking. It is the same clash we saw inside one ברייתא in Step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: But doesn't (he) teach? (introducing a challenge from a ברייתא)
The טרפות that the חכמים listed

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב עָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rav Anan:

phrases.aramaic: מָר אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בָּדֵיק בִּידָא וּמַכְשַׁר,
phrases.english: The master says that Shmuel checks by hand and permits it,
phrases.notes: 'The master' is a polite way of saying 'you,' meaning רב ענן.

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּנָא חַבְרִין אָמַר רַב בָּדֵיק בִּידָא וּמַכְשַׁר.
phrases.english: and our colleague Huna says that Rav checks by hand and permits it.
But doesn't Levi teach:

phrases.aramaic: טְרֵפוֹת שֶׁמָּנוּ חֲכָמִים בִּבְהֵמָה – כְּנֶגְדָּן בָּעוֹף,
phrases.english: The טרפות the Sages listed for an animal apply likewise to a bird,
and beyond those, a bird has one more:

phrases.aramaic: נִשְׁבַּר הָעֶצֶם אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִיקַּב קְרוּם שֶׁל מוֹחַ?
phrases.english: if the bone broke, even though the brain membrane was not pierced?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case where the same contradiction is raised against רב and שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings of שמואל and רב that a bird checked by hand may be permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לוי's ברייתא makes a bird with a broken skull טרפה even when the membrane is whole, so checking should not help.

steps.title: רב ענן: לוי means a water bird with a soft membrane
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן answers that לוי was talking about a water bird; the wording is again fixed to 'its membrane is soft.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That teaching is about a water bird, since it has no membrane. Can you think it has no membrane? Rather, since its membrane is soft.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן gives the same answer as before: לוי's teaching is only about water birds. The גמרא again fixes 'no membrane' to 'a soft membrane.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular birds can still be checked by hand, as רב and שמואל rule. Only a water bird becomes טרפה just from a broken skull, because its soft membrane is assumed to be damaged.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָהוּא בְּעוֹף שֶׁל מַיִם,
phrases.english: He said to him: That is about a water bird,
since it has no membrane.
Can it enter your mind that it has no membrane?
Rather, since its membrane is soft.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָהוּא בְּעוֹף שֶׁל מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge with the same split used in Steps 16-18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases, with a correction of the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוי's rule applies to every bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי's rule is only about a water bird, whose membrane is soft.

steps.title: A hen from רב חנא's house is permitted by רב מתנא
steps.stepSummary: A hen with a broken skull but a whole membrane was brought to רב מתנא, and he permitted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a hen in the house of רב חנא. He sent it to רב מתנא. The bone was broken but the brain membrane was not pierced, and he permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case. This story sets up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנא rules that because the membrane is whole, the hen is kosher even though the skull is broken. This is exactly what לוי's ברייתא seems to forbid.

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא תַּרְנְגוֹלְתָּא דַּהֲוַאי בֵּי רַב חָנָא,
phrases.english: There was a certain hen in the house of Rav Chana;
he sent it before Rav Mattana.

phrases.aramaic: נִשְׁבַּר הָעֶצֶם וְלֹא נִיקַּב קְרוּם שֶׁל מוֹחַ הֲוַאי,
phrases.english: The bone was broken and the brain membrane was not pierced,
and he permitted it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא תַּרְנְגוֹלְתָּא דַּהֲוַאי בֵּי רַב חָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that tests the same question in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hen with a broken skull but a whole membrane was permitted.

steps.title: רב חנא challenges רב מתנא with לוי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא asks how the hen can be kosher when לוי teaches that a broken skull makes a bird טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But לוי teaches: the טרפות the חכמים listed for an animal apply to a bird too, and a bird has one more: a broken bone, even if the brain membrane was not pierced!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנא raises against רב מתנא's ruling the same ברייתא of לוי that רב נחמן used before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hen had exactly the case לוי describes: a broken bone with a whole membrane. So by לוי's teaching it should be טרפה, not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: In addition to them, one more

phrases.english: He said to him: But doesn't Levi teach:
phrases.notes: Here רב חנא, who sent the hen, is the one asking.

phrases.aramaic: טְרֵפוֹת שֶׁמָּנוּ חֲכָמִים בִּבְהֵמָה כְּנֶגְדָּן בָּעוֹף,
phrases.english: The טרפות the Sages listed for an animal apply likewise to a bird,
and beyond those, a bird has one more:

phrases.aramaic: נִשְׁבַּר הָעֶצֶם אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִיקַּב קְרוּם שֶׁל מוֹחַ!
phrases.english: if the bone broke, even though the brain membrane was not pierced!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in the story just told.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנא's permitting of the hen.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לוי's ברייתא says this exact case, a broken bone with a whole membrane, is טרפה.

steps.title: רב מתנא: לוי means a water bird with a soft membrane
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא answers that לוי was talking about a water bird; the wording is fixed to 'its membrane is soft.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There it is about a water bird, since it has no membrane. Can you think it has no membrane? Rather, say: since its membrane is soft.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנא gives the same answer a third time. לוי's rule is only for water birds, and a hen is not a water bird, so it can be checked and permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again the wording 'no membrane' is corrected to 'its membrane is soft.' So the hen, a regular bird with a whole membrane, stays kosher.
steps.whatToRemember: Three times the same answer appears: the rule that a broken skull makes a bird טרפה is only for a water bird, whose membrane is soft. A regular bird, like a hen, can be checked by hand and permitted if the membrane is whole.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם בְּעוֹף שֶׁל מַיִם,
phrases.english: He said to him: There it is about a water bird,
since it has no membrane.
Can it enter your mind that it has no membrane?
Rather, say: since its membrane is soft.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם בְּעוֹף שֶׁל מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חנא's challenge with the same split and wording fix.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases, with a correction of the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוי's rule makes any bird with a broken skull טרפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a water bird with its soft membrane is טרפה from a broken skull; the hen could be checked and permitted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A broken skull alone makes only a water bird טרפה; other birds are checked by hand.

steps.title: Different sages' ways of checking the brain membrane
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists how different אמוראים checked the membrane: רב שיזבי used sunlight, רב יימר used water, and רב אחא בר יעקב had his own method, which the next line describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי would check it by the sun. רב יימר would check it with water. רב אחא בר יעקב would check it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the debate to practice. It reports how different sages actually checked whether the membrane was whole, and the list continues in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps settled that a broken skull with a whole membrane is kosher for an ordinary bird. That leaves a practical question: how do you know the membrane is really whole? Each sage here had his own reliable test.

keyTerms.meaning: The membrane covering the brain, the thing being checked

steps.whyThisMatters: The הלכה depends on whether the membrane is whole, so a dependable way to check it is what makes the rule usable in real life.

phrases.english: Rav Sheizvi would check by the sun;
Rav Yeimar would check with water;
phrases.notes: He poured water in through the hole to see whether it came out mixed with brain tissue.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov would check...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that a whole membrane keeps an ordinary bird kosher, the גמרא gives practical methods for confirming the membrane is whole.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The membrane may be checked by sunlight (רב שיזבי), by water (רב יימר), or by a further method of רב אחא בר יעקב that comes in the next line.
